title.value: Environmental Risk of Psychiatric Disease: A Systematic Review on Air Pollution, Mental Health, and Frontolimbic Brain Regions
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus on environmental risks, specifically air pollution, in relation to psychiatric diseases.
title.quote: P395. Environmental Risk of Psychiatric Disease: A Systematic Review on Air Pollution, Mental Health, and Frontolimbic Brain Regions

extractions.description: This paper is a systematic review examining the effects of air pollution on mental health, particularly regarding anxiety and depression, and exploring its impact on brain regions associated with these conditions.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is the impact of air pollution on mental health and brain structure/function, not climate change itself.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Recent research suggests that air pollution can increase risk of psychopathology, including anxiety and depressive disorders.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the impact of air pollution on mental health and brain function, which falls under the Pollution category.
primary_category.quote: This paper is a systematic review examining the effects of air pollution on mental health...

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not directly relate to other climate change categories beyond pollution.
secondary_categories.quote: The harmful effects of air pollution on respiratory and cardiovascular health are well established, however, its effects on mental health are less clear.

primary_sub_category.justification: Air pollution's impact on mental health is the specific focus of the paper, aligning with the Air Pollution sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: Air pollutants most examined were particulates (PM2.5 - 68%, multiple particulates e 17%, UFP e 14%, PM10 e 1%).

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No other sub-categories are relevant to the paper's focus.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Air pollution was consistently associated with altered structure/function (e.g., increased markers of inflammation, cell death) within the hippocampus, prefrontal cortex, and amygdala.

applications.value: Increased risk of anxiety and depressive disorders due to air pollution
applications.justification: The paper systematically reviews how air pollution increases risk for mental health issues such as anxiety and depression.
applications.quote: Air pollution is associated with increased depression and anxiety symptoms and alterations in brain regions implicated in risk of psychopathology.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing category of Pollution sufficiently covers the paper's focus on air pollution.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The Air Pollution sub-category is appropriate for this paper's focus.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Ninety-one articles on mental health... and 99 on brain structure/function were identified.
